baseline.note: The seed: the repository was created on 2026-10-20 with a README only (main @ ab3d82fe). Nothing is built, so the baseline holds the nine chapters and no requirements; every requirement arrives through a release below. Not yet loaded into Folio.

conventions.kind: release = Niko sees a change; slice = invisible or foundational.
conventions.statements: No screen, route, field, file or product name; one claim; testable.
conventions.numbering: One repository, one version line: Mycelium-LLC/primal-ui. Packages (tokens, css, angular) share the repository's version.
conventions.layers: Primitive, cell and surface are classified by the promise kept, never by size or markup (Niko's brief §3; the book).
conventions.surfaces: Packages tokens, css and angular; the showcase app.

approval.what: Niko approved the plan in session 7F on 2026-10-20 ('plan approved') and 0.1.0 to start. Every later release stays draft until he approves it to start, after his review of the release before it (decision 9).

decisions.ruling: Mycelium Primal is the full name, Primal the short one; tagline 'Design from first principles'; repository Mycelium-LLC/primal-ui (Niko, 2026-10-20). The trademark check is still open.
A plug-and-play design system, and the base every future Mycelium design system is built on; so its look is basic and minimal, made for easy configuration (Niko, 2026-10-20).

One adapter set per framework over a framework-independent core. Only Angular now, 22 and up (22.2.3 is current; 21 is in long-term support). Mac, mobile and others only when Mycelium needs them (Niko, 2026-10-20).
Primitive → cell → surface is the contract, classified by the promise kept: a button is a primitive though interactive; a newsletter signup is a cell (Niko's brief §3).

Private until 1.0.0, then the whole repository flips to public (option A of three: not a public mirror, not public from day one). GitHub cannot make only some branches public, so everything is written from day one as if public (Niko, 2026-10-20).
L2, rung 2: Folio from day one (Niko, 2026-10-20).
Rich text editors, advanced data grids, charts, drag-and-drop builders, complex calendars, maps, file managers, application dashboards (Niko's brief §8).
Decisions, session ids and notes stay in .folio/ when the repository goes public: honest, and it shows how Primal was built ('folio it is', Niko, 2026-10-20).
After each release Niko reviews the newly built chapter or page by hand until it is right, before the next release starts (Niko, 2026-10-20).

0.1.0 starts with the Angular workspace, the showcase shell and the infrastructure, with every planned page present from the start. A page not yet built shows the plain native HTML elements it will cover, and each release replaces its pages with the real ones (Niko, 2026-10-20).

Both, as tokens: a reading container (about 72rem) and full width, so Primal never forces one on a product. The showcase uses the reading container (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'yes both. again this is a base system to expand on').
Primal's own defaults stay minimal and out of the way so products expand on it; Claude decides what is Claude's to decide and asks Niko less (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'minimum interruptions').

Functional and quiet: motion only acknowledges, enters and leaves; short durations, no springs, nothing decorative. Decided by Claude under decision 12; a project adds character through the motion tokens.
Superseded by decision 17. (Was: colour scheme and contrast are independent modes.)
Tokens are authored once in JavaScript data and emitted as CSS custom properties and JSON, so the contrast check reads the same values a product gets. Decided by Claude under decision 12.

Primal is built and shown as a single base, exactly what people get when they import it. No demo or alternative theme ships or appears in the showcase; light, dark, contrast and density are modes of the one base. That a project can re-theme from tokens alone is proven by the token check, not by a second theme (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'why we have 2 themes? we build and work on single base no theme. as people would see when importing the lib').

Primal designs for one solution only: no contrast mode and no density mode. The base has light and dark values and both text directions, nothing else (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'remove contrast and density. we design for one solution only'). Decision 14 is superseded.

Google Sans is Primal's default typeface for English and Hebrew, bundled with the library (Latin, Latin Extended and Hebrew, variable weight 400–700, OFL) so products never call Google Fonts at runtime (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'font to use in the design system by default and imported with the library is google font "google sans" for both languages').

Moving to a new page scrolls to its top, as a switch that is on by default (PrimalPreferences.scrollToTop); back and forward keep the browser's own position, and a link to an anchor goes to the anchor (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'route change scroll to top. as a switch, default on').

A page change is a short cross-fade of the page content, timed by the motion tokens; the shell holds still and nothing slides; instant under reduced motion (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'smoother page transitions please. it jumps').

Every project chooses its black (not necessarily #000), its white (not necessarily #fff) and one primary; every other colour derives from them, and the companion and tertiary come from the primary through a colour-harmony scheme chosen from previews (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'for every project we would choose: whats our black? whats our white? whats our primary? and we can derive rest from this').

Danger, warning, info and success are their own group, outside the harmony, keeping their hues in every project; only their backgrounds mix with the page (Niko, 2026-10-20: 'in another contextual group the system ui colors: like warning | info | sucess? at minimum').

releases.businessMeasure: The base exists: a second theme is made from tokens alone.
releases.name: A base you can make your own
releases.goal: Primal exists as a neutral foundation whose whole look is set by tokens, so it works as it is and any future Mycelium design system starts from it.
releases.usersSee: A live showcase of the single base Primal ships (exactly what a project gets when it imports it), with every token's name and meaning, in light and dark, and switches for the colour scheme and text direction.

items.text: The shell first (decision 10): the showcase with every planned page from the start, each unbuilt page showing the plain native HTML it will cover and the release that builds it.
The Colour page: pick black, white and primary, choose a harmony from live previews (complementary, analogous, triadic, split), see every derived role and its contrast, and copy the theme file.

Repository layout: an Angular CLI workspace. packages/tokens (framework-independent tokens as CSS custom properties, later also JSON), packages/css (reset, base typography and layout in plain CSS), packages/angular (the first adapter, Angular 22+, standalone and zoneless, signals-first), apps/showcase (the live showcase, Angular). CI builds both and checks this ledger.

Semantic tokens: colour from three choices (black, white, primary) and a harmony, every colour role derived in CSS (relative colours, color-mix) and checked by the same model in JavaScript; system colours (danger, warning, info, success) outside the harmony; type scale (fluid), the three gaps, radius, borders, elevation levels with written meanings, layers, motion durations and easing (decisions 21, 22).
Typeface: Google Sans bundled in the core package with its OFL licence, for English and Hebrew (decision 18).
Light and dark: the one base with a value for each colour role in both, following the system and forceable per page or region (decision 17).

primal-angular: PrimalPreferences (theme, direction, scroll to top) and providePrimalRouteScroll: a new page starts at its top, a switch that is on by default; back and forward keep the browser's position (decision 19).
Page changes cross-fade (withPrimalTransitions: the browser's View Transitions, timed by the motion tokens, instant under reduced motion) instead of jumping (decision 20).
Modern reset and base typography; logical properties throughout; reduced motion honoured.
Token check in CI: no component or core style uses a literal colour, length or duration outside the token definitions, so overriding tokens re-themes everything.
Contrast check in CI: every text and control pair, in light and dark, against WCAG 2.2 AA.
Showcase deployed (hosting to be confirmed by Niko); it states the version it shows.
Release chain: release/0.1.0, docs/qa/0.1.0.md, version bump, tag after merge.

releases.rollout: Merged to main by Niko; the showcase is redeployed from main. The repository stays private until 1.0.0, so nobody outside Mycelium sees it.
releases.doneWhen: The showcase, opened by Niko, shows every token in light and dark and both directions; the contrast and token checks pass in CI; the QA table is ✓ by eye; Niko's review of the release is done.

mutations.title: Semantic tokens
mutations.intent: Every value a component uses has a name and a meaning.

mutations.statement: Every colour, type size, gap, radius, border, elevation, layer, duration and density value a component uses comes from a named semantic token, and no component carries a raw value.
mutations.success: A search of every component's styles finds no literal colour, length or duration outside the token definitions.
mutations.disqualifier: Any component hardcodes a value that a theme cannot reach.

mutations.statement: Spacing is three gaps that clearly contrast: between sections, between elements of a group, and inside a component.
mutations.success: Every gap in every component maps to one of the three gap tokens, and the three are visibly different at a glance.
mutations.disqualifier: A gap is chosen by eye, or two of the three gaps read as the same size.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §1.3

mutations.statement: Every elevation level, border and fill treatment has a written meaning, and none is used only for decoration.
mutations.success: The token reference completes 'this style means: …' for each treatment, and each use in a component matches its sentence.
mutations.disqualifier: A treatment exists without its sentence, or a box is drawn only because the page felt unfinished.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §1.4–1.5

mutations.statement: The type scale is fluid between phone and desk widths and keeps body text within a readable line length.
mutations.success: From 320 to 1920 pixels wide, headings and body scale without a jump, and body lines stay between about 45 and 80 characters.
mutations.disqualifier: Text sizes jump at breakpoints, or body text runs edge to edge on a wide screen.

mutations.title: Themes and configuration
mutations.intent: One structure, any look.

mutations.statement: A designer creates a complete new theme for a project by overriding tokens only, without forking or editing any component.
mutations.success: Overriding tokens in one file loaded after Primal's changes the look of every page, and the build check finds no component or core style using a value outside the tokens.
mutations.disqualifier: Any part of a new look needs a component change, a copied component or a style that targets a component's internals; or the build check finds a literal value.
mutations.role: a designer starting a new Mycelium design system
mutations.action: start the project's design system from Primal
mutations.outcome: I get my own look with all of Primal's behaviour, without maintaining a fork

mutations.statement: Light and dark ship as values of the one base, follow the system preference by default, and can be forced for a page or a region of it.
mutations.success: With the system preference set to each, the matching scheme shows; a forced region keeps its scheme inside a page in the other.
mutations.disqualifier: The scheme ignores the system preference, or forcing a region changes the whole page.

mutations.statement: Primal's own look is minimal and carries no brand, so its default is a quiet starting point rather than a finished identity.
mutations.success: The default theme uses no Mycelium colour, mark or typeface, and its components read as finished but plain.
mutations.disqualifier: The default look is recognisably a Mycelium product, or a project has to remove styling before adding its own.
mutations.evidence: Niko, 2026-10-20: 'basic and minimal design to allow for easy configuration'; the base for any future Mycelium design system.

mutations.title: Both directions, quiet motion
mutations.intent: Right-to-left and reduced motion are not afterthoughts.

mutations.statement: Every component is laid out with logical properties, so it works right-to-left and left-to-right without separate styles.
mutations.success: Every showcase page switched to right-to-left mirrors correctly, and any direction-specific style is listed with why logical properties could not do it.
mutations.disqualifier: A component breaks or keeps left-to-right order when the direction is right-to-left.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Niko's standing rule on logical CSS properties (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md).

mutations.statement: When the person asks for reduced motion, nothing moves except what is needed to understand a change.
mutations.success: With reduced motion on, every showcase transition is instant or a cross-fade, and nothing loops.
mutations.disqualifier: Any slide, bounce, parallax or loop plays with reduced motion on.

mutations.statement: All text and controls meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in light and in dark, checked automatically.
mutations.success: The contrast check covers every foreground and background pair in light and dark and fails the build on any miss.
mutations.disqualifier: A pair below AA ships, or the check is run by hand only.

mutations.title: One core, an adapter per framework
mutations.intent: The look and the contracts belong to no framework.

mutations.statement: Tokens, styles and contracts work with no framework at all, and each framework gets its own adapter set that adds behaviour without redefining the look.
mutations.success: A plain HTML page using only the core styles renders the foundation the same way the first adapter's showcase does.
mutations.disqualifier: A visual rule exists only inside an adapter, or the core needs a framework to render.
mutations.evidence: Niko, 2026-10-20: 'a set per framework. currently supporting only angular 22+… later for all the mac apps and mobile… when we would need it'.

mutations.title: The live showcase
mutations.intent: See it working, not described.

mutations.statement: A person opens the live showcase, sees every foundation token and theme, and switches theme and text direction in place.
mutations.success: From the showcase, every token is visible with its name and meaning, and switching the colour scheme or direction changes the whole page at once without a reload.
mutations.disqualifier: A token is missing, a switch needs a reload, or the showcase shows anything not built.
mutations.role: a designer or developer at Mycelium
mutations.action: look at Primal before using it
mutations.outcome: I know what I get and how it changes

releases.businessMeasure: Plain content needs no styling work.
releases.name: Plain HTML reads right
releases.status: Draft; starts after Niko's review of the release before it.
releases.goal: Anything written as plain HTML or Markdown is readable, well spaced and accessible with no classes, and every element of the standard has a decided outcome.
releases.usersSee: A showcase section rendering every rendering HTML element unstyled-by-author (text, lists, quotes, code, tables, media, landmarks, bidirectional text), and the coverage inventory with each element's outcome and reason.

items.text: The coverage inventory: every rendering element of the HTML living standard, each marked styled, enhanced by a component, or left native, with why. Infrastructure elements (script, style, meta, link, head, title) and deprecated ones are listed as excluded.

Classless base for text and document semantics, lists and definitions, quotes, technical content (code, pre, kbd, samp, var), revisions and highlights, metadata (time, data, address), bidirectional and ruby text.
Page structure: landmarks (header, main, nav, aside, footer, section, article, search, hgroup) documented with their accessibility roles.
Table foundation: caption, regions, numeric alignment, sticky header, overflow inside the table, empty state.
Media: responsive images and picture, figure with caption, audio and video with native controls and tracks, responsive iframe embeds, svg and canvas sizing and labelling.
Release chain for 0.2.0.

releases.rollout: Merged to main by Niko; the showcase is redeployed from main. The repository stays private until 1.0.0, so nobody outside Mycelium sees it.
releases.doneWhen: A Markdown document and a long plain-HTML article render well in all three themes and both directions with no classes; the inventory has no unaccounted element; QA ✓ by eye.

mutations.title: Every element accounted for
mutations.intent: The standard is the audit.

mutations.statement: Every rendering element of the HTML standard has a recorded outcome (styled, enhanced by a component, or deliberately left native) with its reason.
mutations.success: The coverage inventory lists every rendering element of the living standard, and none is unaccounted for.
mutations.disqualifier: An element renders with unreviewed browser defaults, or is missing from the inventory.

mutations.statement: Native behaviour is kept wherever it serves the person better than a custom replacement, and a custom control replaces a native one only with a written reason.
mutations.success: Every component that replaces a native control names, in its contract, what the native one could not do.
mutations.disqualifier: A native control is replaced only to look branded (for example a custom calendar where the native date input serves).

mutations.title: Plain HTML reads right
mutations.intent: Content with no classes is already good.

mutations.statement: Content written as plain HTML or Markdown, with no classes, is readable, well spaced and accessible: headings, text, lists, quotes, code, media and page landmarks.
mutations.success: A long Markdown document rendered with only Primal's core styles has a clear heading hierarchy, readable spacing and no element at browser defaults.
mutations.disqualifier: Any common element needs a class to look right.

mutations.statement: Mixed-direction and language-specific text (isolated runs, ruby annotations) renders correctly inside content of either direction.
mutations.success: A right-to-left paragraph with embedded left-to-right names and numbers, and a ruby annotation, render in the right order.
mutations.disqualifier: Embedded opposite-direction text reorders its neighbours, or ruby text overlaps.

mutations.title: Tables
mutations.intent: Data you can read down and across.

mutations.statement: Tables align numbers on a common edge, keep their header in view while scrolling, scroll sideways within themselves on narrow widths, and say so when they are empty.
mutations.success: A 40-row numeric table at phone and desk widths keeps its header visible, its numbers aligned, scrolls only inside itself, and its empty version says why it is empty.
mutations.disqualifier: The page scrolls sideways because of a table, numbers are ragged, or an empty table shows only headers.

mutations.title: Media
mutations.intent: Media holds its place and says what it is.

mutations.statement: Media keeps its aspect ratio while loading, never overflows its container, and has a text alternative or is marked decorative.
mutations.success: Images, video and embeds reserve their space before loading (no layout shift), fit their container at every width, and each has alternative text or an explicit decorative mark.
mutations.disqualifier: Content jumps when media loads, media overflows, or an image has no alternative and no decorative mark.

releases.businessMeasure: Forms need no custom field work.
releases.name: Fields that never leave you guessing
releases.status: Draft; starts after Niko's review of the release before it.
releases.goal: Every native form element is covered by a field primitive with one contract: label, description, required or optional, disabled, read-only, error, keyboard.
releases.usersSee: A showcase of every field in every state, three example forms (sign-in, profile edit, settings) built only from Primal, and their validation in action.

items.text: Field primitives: TextField (text, email, password, tel, url, search), NumberField, date and time fields (native inputs), Checkbox, Radio and RadioGroup, Switch, Slider, ColorField, FileField, TextArea, Select, OutputValue, Progress and Meter as display.
Composition: FieldLabel, FormField (label, description, control, message), FieldGroup (fieldset and legend), ValidationMessage.
Validation contract: when errors appear (on leaving a field, on submit), where, how they are announced, how they clear.
Angular adapter: the field primitives as standalone components working with Angular forms, plus the same markup documented for plain HTML.
Release chain for 0.3.0.

releases.rollout: Merged to main by Niko; the showcase is redeployed from main. The repository stays private until 1.0.0, so nobody outside Mycelium sees it.
releases.doneWhen: The three example forms work by keyboard alone and with a screen reader, every field shows every state, and QA ✓ by eye in all themes and both directions.

mutations.title: Fields
mutations.intent: Each native input, one contract.

mutations.statement: Every field has a visible label, an optional description, a required or optional state, disabled and read-only states, and an error state, all exposed to assistive technology.
mutations.success: For every field primitive, each state is visible and announced by a screen reader with the label and description.
mutations.disqualifier: A field without a visible label exists, or a state is shown only visually.

mutations.statement: Each native field type (the text kinds, number, date and time, checkbox, radio, range, colour, file, select and text area) is covered by a field primitive that keeps the browser's own input behaviour.
mutations.success: Every native type has its primitive, and its native keyboard, picker and autofill behaviour still work.
mutations.disqualifier: A native type has no primitive, or a primitive breaks native autofill, pickers or keyboard input.

mutations.statement: Related fields group under a shared legend, and a radio group is one stop in the tab order that moves by arrow keys.
mutations.success: Tabbing reaches a radio group once, arrows move the choice, and the group's legend is announced.
mutations.disqualifier: Each radio is its own tab stop, or a group has no announced name.

mutations.statement: A switch or toggle says what it changes, in words, rather than only on or off.
mutations.success: Every switch example in the showcase is labelled with its consequence ('Email me when a report is ready'), and the pattern is in its contract.
mutations.disqualifier: A switch is labelled 'Enabled', or its effect is only implied.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §0.6 (configuration forms show the consequence).

mutations.title: Validation
mutations.intent: An error tells you what to type.

mutations.statement: A field's error says what happened and what to type, sits directly under its field, and is announced when it appears.
mutations.success: In the example forms, every error is under its field, readable as an instruction, announced once, and gone when fixed.
mutations.disqualifier: An error shows in a banner or toast, says only 'invalid', or is not announced.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §2.2, §3.2

mutations.title: Forms from Primal alone
mutations.intent: A whole form without inventing a field.

mutations.statement: A developer builds a sign-in, a profile edit and a settings form using only Primal's field primitives and form composition, with no custom field styling.
mutations.success: The three example forms exist in the showcase with no style written outside Primal.
mutations.disqualifier: Any of the three needs a custom style or a field that Primal does not provide.
mutations.role: a developer on a Mycelium project
mutations.outcome: it is consistent and accessible without my own field code

releases.name: Every action answers
releases.status: Draft; starts after Niko's review of the release before it.
releases.goal: Actions and their feedback follow one written behaviour model, so every action is acknowledged, its outcome is specific, and its weight matches what it did.
releases.usersSee: Buttons, links and button groups in every state; alerts, toasts, spinners, progress and skeletons; and a page that walks through each action kind with its gate, sequence, weight and undo.

items.text: Actions: Button, IconButton, Link (internal, external, download), ButtonGroup.
Feedback: Alert, Toast, Spinner, Progress, Skeleton.
The behaviour model written once: the three facts (what it is, who says it, what it wants), the fixed set of places, and what each place means.
Action kinds written once (destructive, constructive, mutative, navigational, background, confirmatory; reversible or not), each with gate, sequence, weight, reversibility window and error contract.
Release chain for 0.4.0.

releases.rollout: Merged to main by Niko; the showcase is redeployed from main. The repository stays private until 1.0.0, so nobody outside Mycelium sees it.
releases.doneWhen: Every action in the showcase acknowledges within 100 ms and shows its outcome where the eye is; a destructive example has distance and undo; QA ✓ by eye.

mutations.title: Actions
mutations.intent: Something happens, and you know what.

mutations.statement: A button's label names the action with the person's verb and an object, and a pending button cannot be activated twice.
mutations.success: Every button in the showcase reads verb plus object ('Save Changes'), and a pending button ignores a second activation while showing that it is working.
mutations.disqualifier: A label reads 'Submit' or 'OK', or a double activation sends twice.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Niko's standing rule on button labels (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md).

mutations.statement: A destructive action never sits as a peer of safe ones: it has its own distance and treatment.
mutations.success: In every example with a destructive action, it is separated from Save and Cancel by the section gap and has the destructive treatment.
mutations.disqualifier: A delete sits in the same group, at the same weight, as a safe action.

mutations.title: Feedback
mutations.intent: Waiting and results, shown honestly.

mutations.statement: Loading shows the shape of what is coming when the shape is known, and a progress value when the length is known.
mutations.success: Lists load as skeletons of their rows, measurable work shows a percentage, and a spinner appears only when neither is known.
mutations.disqualifier: A spinner hides a known shape or length, or progress is faked.

mutations.title: The feedback contract
mutations.intent: Silence is a message.

mutations.statement: Every action is acknowledged within 100 ms, then states its specific outcome where the person's eyes already are.
mutations.success: Every interactive example responds visibly within 100 ms, and its outcome names what happened at the place of the action.
mutations.disqualifier: An action shows nothing at first, or its outcome is generic ('Success') or shown far from the action.

mutations.statement: Feedback weight follows one ladder: irreversible actions are impossible to miss, constructive ones are clear without interrupting, background ones are glance-sized and fade, and routine ones only acknowledge.
mutations.success: Each showcase example's feedback matches its rung, and no routine action raises a toast.
mutations.disqualifier: A routine action shouts, or an irreversible one passes quietly.

mutations.statement: Where a message goes is decided by what it is, who is saying it and what it wants from the person, from a small fixed set of places, each with one meaning.
mutations.success: The behaviour model lists the places and their meanings, and every feedback component documents which place it is.
mutations.disqualifier: A component picks a toast or banner by taste.

mutations.title: Action kinds
mutations.intent: Decided once, in plain words.

mutations.statement: Each action kind (destructive, constructive, mutative, navigational, background, confirmatory) has a written gate, sequence, weight, reversibility window and error contract that every component follows.
mutations.success: The action-kind page states all five for each kind in plain words, and every action component names its kind.
mutations.disqualifier: An action behaves differently from its kind's written contract.

releases.businessMeasure: Nobody gets lost or stuck in a layer.
releases.name: You always know where you are
releases.status: Draft; starts after Niko's review of the release before it.
releases.goal: Moving around and opening things on top follow written rules: navigation only moves, each top layer keeps its claim, and focus is never lost.
releases.usersSee: Tabs, breadcrumbs, pagination, menus and navigation items; dialogs, popovers, tooltips and accordions; keyboard paths through each, with focus visible and returning where it should.

items.text: Navigation: Tabs, Breadcrumbs, Pagination, Menu, NavigationItem.
Disclosure and top layers on the native foundations (dialog, popover, details): Dialog (including confirmation), Popover, Tooltip, Accordion.
The seven top-layer answers written once: what earns a modal, beside versus over, what is a place, which layers get addresses, stacking, what returns on close, what each becomes on a phone.
Physics: visible focus, reading-order focus, defined return targets, Escape for the topmost layer, keyboard path for every component.
Release chain for 0.5.0.

releases.rollout: Merged to main by Niko; the showcase is redeployed from main. The repository stays private until 1.0.0, so nobody outside Mycelium sees it.
releases.doneWhen: Every navigation and top-layer example works by keyboard alone with focus always visible and returning correctly; QA ✓ by eye.

mutations.title: Navigation
mutations.intent: Navigation moves you; actions do something.

mutations.statement: Navigation only moves the person and never filters, toggles or creates: tabs switch faces of the same thing, breadcrumbs go up a real hierarchy, and back follows the step actually taken.
mutations.success: No navigation component in Primal performs an action, and each documents which of the three moves it is.
mutations.disqualifier: A navigation item filters, toggles or creates, or tabs hold unrelated places.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §1.7

mutations.title: Top layers
mutations.intent: Each layer keeps its claim.

mutations.statement: A dialog interrupts, returns the page exactly as it was left, always has a way out that isn't the answer, and is not a place.
mutations.success: Closing a dialog restores scroll, selection and focus; every dialog has a dismiss that is not its confirm; browser back never lands inside one.
mutations.disqualifier: A dialog changes the page under it, has no way out but the answer, or traps back navigation.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §1.9

mutations.statement: A panel, popover or tooltip leaves the page the person's own, and closing it returns focus to what opened it.
mutations.success: With a popover open the page still scrolls and reads; on close, focus is back on its trigger.
mutations.disqualifier: A popover blocks the page, or closing it drops focus to the top of the document.

mutations.statement: A disclosure keeps its open state where it is shown, and opening one never moves what the person is reading.
mutations.success: Opening an accordion section above the reading position keeps the reading position in place.
mutations.disqualifier: Opening a section scrolls or shifts the content being read.

mutations.title: Physics
mutations.intent: Keys and focus you can trust.

mutations.statement: Focus is always visible, moves in reading order, and has a defined destination when any layer closes, and Escape closes the topmost layer.
mutations.success: Tabbing through every showcase page shows focus on every stop, in reading order, and Escape closes only the topmost layer.
mutations.disqualifier: Focus is invisible anywhere, jumps out of order, or Escape closes more than one layer.

mutations.statement: Every component's journey works from the keyboard alone.

mutations.title: Information
mutations.intent: Nature and state before words.

mutations.statement: A card is a list item: it appears only as one of several siblings that are each something you open or act on, never as a single child or a page container.
mutations.success: Every card example in Primal is one of at least two siblings and is openable or actionable; the contract forbids the single-card and card-as-page uses.
mutations.disqualifier: A card wraps a whole page, a section, or a lone piece of content.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); UI Design Course ch. 01 (the card contract) and ch. 00 (minimum siblings).

mutations.statement: Status, badges and indicators carry their meaning in shape or text as well as colour, and no fact appears twice in one item.
mutations.success: With colour removed, every status in the showcase still reads; no item shows the same status as both a dot and a word.
mutations.disqualifier: A status is colour only, or an item repeats a fact.

mutations.statement: An empty state says why it is empty and offers the next step, in the place the content would be.
mutations.success: Every list, table and search example has an empty version that names the reason and the next action in place.
mutations.disqualifier: An empty state is a blank area, a generic illustration, or appears somewhere other than where the content goes.

mutations.title: Layout
mutations.intent: Group by space and alignment.

mutations.statement: Layout helpers (stack, inline, grid, container, divider, scroll area) group by space and alignment, and draw a line only where a written treatment says so.
mutations.success: With borders, fills and shadows removed, every showcase layout still reads its grouping and rank.
mutations.disqualifier: Grouping depends on boxes, or a line has no written meaning.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §1.4 (strip test).

mutations.title: Cells keep their payload
mutations.intent: The one thing a cell exists to show stays.

mutations.statement: Every cell names its payload, and when room runs out the payload stays while labels, chips and metadata give way.
mutations.success: At 320 pixels wide with real-length data, every cell still shows its payload in full or with a deliberate truncation.
mutations.disqualifier: Metadata survives while the payload is cut, or a cell has no named payload.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §1.2

mutations.statement: Each cell shipped with Primal fulfils one complete job end to end, including its feedback.
mutations.success: Each cell's contract names its job and its demo completes that job with its feedback (for example, subscribe ends in a confirmed subscription or a fixable error).
mutations.disqualifier: A cell stops before its job is done, or leaves feedback to the page around it.

mutations.title: The contract catalog
mutations.intent: What am I promising, and did I keep it?

mutations.statement: Every primitive, cell and surface documents its contract: promise, behaviour, context, relationships, states, accessibility and failure conditions.
mutations.success: The build fails if any component lacks a contract or any of its seven parts.
mutations.disqualifier: A component ships without a complete contract.

mutations.statement: Each component is classified as primitive, cell or surface by the promise it keeps, not by its size or markup, and the reason is written.
mutations.success: Every contract states its layer and why, and a button, for example, is a primitive although it is interactive.
mutations.disqualifier: A component is classified by how big or how nested it is.
mutations.evidence: Niko's v1 brief, 2026-10-20 (session 7F-primal-foundation) (§3, the architectural correction); Thoughts on Design and Humanity, via ~/.claude/guides/design-system-guides/01-design-system.md §1.1

mutations.statement: Contracts are kept as framework-independent data next to the components, and the documentation is generated from them, so the two cannot drift.
mutations.success: Changing a contract changes its documentation page on the next build, with nothing written by hand in between.
mutations.disqualifier: Documentation is written separately from the contract, or a contract lives inside one framework's code.

mutations.statement: Every contract answers three questions: what it promises, what its presence makes someone expect, and how it shows whether it kept the promise.
mutations.success: The three answers are present and specific in every contract.
mutations.disqualifier: Any answer is missing or generic.

questionsForNiko.question: Is 'Mycelium Primal' clear of existing use and trademarks?
questionsForNiko.why: Needed before the repository goes public at 1.0.0; Niko named it the one step left before committing to the name.

questionsForNiko.question: Which npm scope publishes the packages: @mycelium (not known to be ours) or @mycelium-llc (the estate's), and on npm or GitHub Packages?
questionsForNiko.why: The brief suggests @mycelium/primal; npm shows no such packages and this Mac cannot tell who owns the @mycelium scope.

questionsForNiko.question: Which license: MIT (recommended) or Apache-2.0?
questionsForNiko.why: The brief asks for a permissive license; MIT is the simplest, Apache-2.0 adds a patent grant.

questionsForNiko.question: Where is the showcase hosted while the repository is private?
questionsForNiko.why: 0.1.0's done-when needs a live showcase Niko can open; Firebase Hosting in an existing Mycelium project is the usual path.

notPlanned.reason: Excluded from v1 (Niko's brief §8): rich text editors, advanced data grids, charts, drag-and-drop builders, complex calendars, maps, file managers and application dashboards. They should be possible on Primal later, but they are not part of the foundation.
Adapters beyond Angular (Mac, mobile, other web frameworks): when a Mycelium product needs one (Niko, 2026-10-20).
